name: samba
desc: SMB/CIFS file, print, and login server for UNIX
why: A door into SMB/CIFS, the Windows file-sharing protocol that runs quietly in most networks and is rarely examined.

brief.what_it_is: Samba is a free, open source implementation of the SMB/CIFS file-sharing and print protocols, plus Active Directory-related protocols such as LDAP and Kerberos, for Linux and UNIX-like systems. It lets Linux and Unix machines serve file and print shares to Windows and other SMB clients, and it can act as an Active Directory Domain Controller or as a member server. The formula ships a server daemon (smbd, nmbd) and a large set of client and admin tools (smbclient, net, testparm, smbstatus, rpcclient, and others). The homepage also describes uses in cluster filesystems, PaaS and software-defined storage, HPC, and NAS.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage frames Samba as a way to integrate Linux/Unix servers and desktops into Windows and Active Directory environments, providing secure, stable and fast file and print services to clients using SMB and related AD protocols.
brief.install_notes: Homebrew caveats: to avoid conflicting with macOS system binaries, smbd is installed as $HOMEBREW_PREFIX/sbin/samba-dot-org-smbd and profiles as $HOMEBREW_PREFIX/bin/samba-dot-org-profiles. No other install steps, accounts, or first-run configuration were seen on the pages fetched.
brief.standout: Samba is one of the few pieces of open source software that lets a non-Windows box sit inside a Windows Active Directory domain as a full domain controller, not just a file share. The package bundles a large toolkit (over 40 executables in the formula) covering server, client, registry, and LDAP-style database tools.
brief.status: Maintained. The homepage lists Samba 4.25.0 as the current stable release, with news items dated 12 October 2026 (Samba 4.24.8) and 1 October 2026 (Samba 4.23.13), and it notes the project is developed, maintained and supported by an active worldwide community. The homepage also carries a dated memorial notice for a team member.
brief.caveats: The homepage and docs index contain no command examples, so commands_seen is empty. The docs page says the man pages come from the development version and may differ from older releases. Installed names for smbd and profiles differ on Homebrew to avoid clashing with macOS binaries. Licensing is GNU GPL. The docs index links to a Samba Wiki that I did not fetch, so I have not verified its current contents.
quotes: Samba is the most feature-rich Open Source implementation of the SMB and Active Directory protocols for Linux and UNIX-like systems.
Opening Windows to a Wider World
Samba is Free Software licensed under the GNU General Public License, the Samba project is a member of the Software Freedom Conservancy.
